title: Phase-One Success Return Path
statement: Let $E,s,w,i$ be natural numbers with $s\le w$ and $i+1\le w$, let $\mathrm{orc}:\mathrm{Fin}(4)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})\to\mathrm{Bool}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a Boolean list, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a machine state satisfying the invariant $\mathrm{Inv}(s,w,i+1,\mathrm{st})$. For every $M_2\le 2^w$, the machine $A(E)$ has a finite run from the configuration whose control state is the phase-one success state, whose registers agree with $\mathrm{st}$ except that $U=M$, $M=M_2$, and $E$ equals the original value of $U$, and whose result is unset, to the configuration whose control state is the successful return state and whose registers agree with $\mathrm{st}$ except that $M=M_2$, again with unset result; throughout the run, every configuration before the final one satisfies the input precondition and has all registers at most $2^{w^2}$.
